newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open higher Friday following May's expiry and early talk of firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from about $2.15 to $2.18 after settling Thursday at $2.122 per million British thermal units.
In ACCESS, June last traded 3.8 cents higher at $2.16.
"There's a continued squeeze in the physical market," one market source said, noting early weekend cash prices were talked in the low-$2.20s on Transco (Station 65).
Technical traders pegged important support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area. Resistance was seen in the low-$2.20s and then at $2.33.

In Thursday's cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded more than 10 cents to about $2.05-10. Midcontinent pipes were down a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at New York city gate also stumbled more than 10 cents to $2.35-40.
Early Appalachian cash prices for the weekend on Columbia Gas were talked slightly higher in the mid-$2.30s.
Temperatures throughout most of the U.S. are expected to run near to slightly above normal through the weekend, with cooler-than-normal weather expected to cover the Southwest Saturday.
